docs.valued.component: `Valued` is the element's own game data, as plain fields: a rank, a suit, a cost — whatever a
RULE will read. The atom stores and never interprets; the readers are the rule language
(`el.values.rank` in an `Acceptor`), sorting, and scoring. Values are spec — they live on the
node and cross the wire — and they are the reason a card IS the seven of spades rather than a
// a zone that takes sevens reads the atom through the rule language:
## The atom stores, the rule reads
No method on the card answers "am I a seven" — the QUESTION belongs to whoever asks it: an
accept rule compares `el.values.rank`, a scorer sums costs, a sorter orders by rank. One store,
many readers, and adding a reader never touches the atom.
docs.valued.rank: One card, one number. The zone takes rank 7 and nothing else; the `rank` knob writes the card's
`values`. Drag the card at the zone: at 7 it lights, at anything else it stays dark — the rule
reads `el.values.rank` off this very atom, and no other code path knows what a rank is.
